sections.title: Act on Data Protection and the Protection of Privacy in Telecommunications and Digital Services (TDDDG)

questions.question: May an amateur station be used to eavesdrop on private (non-public) conversations?
questions.answer_a: Eavesdropping on private (non-public) conversations is a criminal offence.
questions.answer_b: The operator of an amateur station counts as a competent person and may therefore decide which frequencies to listen on.
questions.answer_c: Eavesdropping on private (non-public) conversations requires a special authorisation from the BNetzA.
questions.answer_d: Anyone is entitled to do so if technically approved receivers are used.

questions.question: By which action is the secrecy of telecommunications violated?
questions.answer_a: By receiving, using or passing on messages that are not intended for radio amateurs, the general public or an unspecified group of people.
questions.answer_b: By using or passing on conversation content and data from amateur radio contacts in which the radio amateur did not take part.
questions.answer_c: By using or passing on conversation content and data from amateur radio contacts, regardless of whether the radio amateur took part.
questions.answer_d: By recording and passing on conversation content and data from amateur radio contacts, in particular if they are passed on to persons who are not radio amateurs.

questions.question: What must a person do on receiving messages that are <u>not</u> intended for radio amateurs, the general public or an unspecified group of people?
questions.answer_a: Neither the content of the messages nor the fact that they were received may be communicated to others. This does not apply in emergencies and disasters.
questions.answer_b: The fact of reception may be communicated to third parties, but not the content and the details. This also applies in emergencies and disasters.
questions.answer_c: The fact of reception may be communicated to other radio amateurs, but not the content.
questions.answer_d: The receiver must be switched off immediately and the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) informed.
